Hi Jordan — great questions. Short answers below; Dev will follow up with details and the filled questionnaire.

- Cloud providers: Redwood’s hosted offering runs primarily in AWS (us-west-2) for US tenants; we also have regions on GCP for certain customers and partner regions in EU. For enterprise/Dedicated customers we support customer-managed VPCs and on-prem deployments to ensure residency.
- Logs & telemetry: our default telemetry collects anonymized request metrics, token counts, latencies, and service traces. Customer-supplied content (prompts/responses) is treated as customer data; we do not index or use it for training. Logs may contain message IDs and non-PII metadata. If customers send PII in prompts, that content is stored only in the context of the request/response lifecycle and retained according to the customer-configured retention policy; we offer short retention windows and configurable redaction.
- SOC 2: yes, this is a SOC 2 Type II report (covering period 2024-09-01 through 2025-08-31). The full report is available under NDA; summary attached.

Attachment: vendor_questionnaire_acme_initial.xlsx (initial template — Dev will fill technical sections).

Next steps: Dev, can you take the lead on the questionnaire and provide the detailed subprocessor breakdown (including KMS, monitoring, analytics vendors)? Jordan — we’ll propose times for Fri 6/18.

—
Marissa

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the questions. I’ve filled the initial pass of the questionnaire (attached) and added a more detailed subprocessor CSV. Short answers inline: 

- Cloud providers: Primary compute & model serving on AWS (EC2, EKS, S3). We also leverage GCP for select regions (BigQuery for analytics in EU). Customers can opt for Dedicated pools in a single cloud or Private deployments in their VPC.
- Data flows & PII: Customer inputs and generated outputs are handled as customer data. For Hosted customers we store request/response contexts in encrypted stores for the configured retention window; by default retention is 30 days for recent evals and 90 days for troubleshooting traces, but enterprise customers can request custom retention or zero-retention modes. Logs used for monitoring are scrubbed of full prompt text by default; we maintain only metadata and telemetry.
- KMS & keys: We use customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS for enterprise customers; for hosted customers we use Redwood-managed keys in AWS KMS with strict access controls.

I’ve attached: redwood_subprocessors_detailed.csv and a filled vendor_questionnaire_acme_initial.xlsx (initial responses). We can expand any field you want and provide additional evidence under NDA.

Regards,

Hi Sarah / Jordan —

Quick answers and next steps (we’ll expand any items on the follow-up call):
- Third-party monitoring: We use Datadog for metrics and traces; Datadog receives telemetry and metadata only. Raw request/response bodies are not forwarded to third-party monitoring by default. We can provide configuration screenshots and export controls on the call.
- KMS/HSM: For hosted customers we use AWS KMS with strict key access policies; enterprise customers can bring their own CMK or HSM via AWS CloudHSM integrations.
- Onboarding timeline: Private/VPC onboarding is typically 4–8 weeks depending on network approvals and testing. We can provide a mutual action plan for an accelerated path.
- DPA: attaching our standard DPA for initial review and a DocuSign link for execution if helpful.
